description:
## Problem

The ScentLeakage rule treats any variable carrying a URL or identifier as potentially sensitive (scent) without distinguishing actual secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords) from public data (feed URLs, API endpoints, config paths).

## Evidence

From quickheadlines scan (2026-06-01):
- 137 ScentLeakage findings, all on public feed URLs from config files
- Feed URLs are public data served to clients, not secrets

## Example

```crystal
# Flagged as scent leakage but these are just public feed URLs
QuickHeadlines::Services::StoryService.get_timeline(allowed_feed_urls)
```

## Expected Behavior

The ScentLeakage rule should only flag data that is plausibly secret: API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, credentials. Public URLs, endpoints, and identifiers should not trigger scent warnings.

## Suggested Fix

1. Narrow scent detection to known secret patterns (env vars with KEY/SECRET/TOKEN/PASSWORD, hardcoded credentials, etc.)
2. Do not flag URL-type data as scent by default -- URLs are inherently public identifiers.
3. Consider an allowlist of variable patterns that are known non-secrets (*_url, *_path, *_uri, feed_*, config_*).
title: ScentLeakage rule: distinguish public data from actual secrets
